result.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?
result.summary: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. To this end, this paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources, where we consider either stationary and ergodic non-Markovian sources or those which are hidden Markov models of some finite order (possibly non-stationary). In either case, we first obtain error bounds via finite models with finite window approximations. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate $α^{\lfloor M/N\rfloor}$, where $M$ is the window length and $α$ is determined by filter stability (and the Dobrushin coefficients of the transition and measurement kernels). We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$, one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastic control developed in earlier work, which rigorously returns a near optimal Transformer. In particular, we show that for a non-Markovian source, either under stationarity and ergodicity for general models or under filter stability for hidden Markov models, an optimally trained Transformer has arbitrarily small performance error with increasing context length, data, and approximation refinement. Numerical studies accompany the theory.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从随机最优控制角度理论分析 Transformer 对非马尔可夫源的下一 token 预测，用有限窗口与截断滤波近似给出误差界，并构造深度 M+1、每层单头的 Transformer 实现截断滤波，证明最优训练后误差可随上下文长度、数据和近似精度趋于任意小。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「内部状态需承载历史充分统计量」的截断滤波视角，可能为 LVR 中 latent 是否保留任务必要信息及长度泛化提供理论参照；但该文不涉及视觉或推理期 latent 生成，可供核查其可迁移性。
